RagShortTexts: Granada maintained autonomy by paying massive annual gold parias tribute to the Crown of Castile.

Variants.Content: Under the 1246 Treaty of Jaén, the Nasrid Emirate of Granada preserved its sovereignty by paying massive annual parias in pure gold to Castile. Benefiting from trans-Saharan caravan gold dust routes and luxury silk manufacture, Granada's tribute paradoxically financed the very Castilian military apparatus encircling it.

Castilian grandees continually weigh military conquest against the steady harvest of Islamic gold dinars. The annual paria operates as a golden leash, draining Moorish treasury reserves without requiring costly sieges.
Granadan silk weavers work by lamplight, knowing seven copper dirhams of every ten are melted into bullion for Toledo. Whenever the Castilian king threatens war, taxes double across the vega.
